questions.prompt: When drafting a job description with AI, what input produces the most useful output?
choices: The job title and a list of responsibilities copied from the previous holder's LinkedIn
The role's expected outcomes at 6 months, plus must-have versus nice-to-have skills
A brief description of the team culture and preferred personality type
The internal compensation band and leveling criteria for the role
questions.explanation: Outcome-based inputs — what the person needs to achieve and the real skills bar — give AI the specifics it needs to write something useful. Job titles pull toward boilerplate; internal comp data should never go into a public model.

questions.prompt: An AI bias review flags the phrase 'we move fast and break things' in a job description. What is the most likely concern?
choices: The phrase is trademarked and cannot be used without permission
It implies a pace that may discourage applicants with caregiving responsibilities or disabilities
It is too informal and will make the company look unprofessional to senior candidates
It describes an illegal practice under most employment laws
questions.explanation: Culture-coded phrases like 'move fast and break things' often signal a specific archetype — typically young, unencumbered, high-hours — that can discourage applicants with caregiving responsibilities, health considerations, or simply different working styles. It is a common inclusion-narrowing signal.

questions.prompt: Which piece of information should you NOT paste into a public AI model when drafting a job description?
choices: The outcomes you expect from the role in the first six months
A list of tools and technologies the role uses
Your company's internal salary bands and leveling criteria
A description of the team the role will join
questions.explanation: Internal salary bands and leveling guides are confidential. Pasting them into a public model risks exposing compensation strategy. You can describe the level functionally — years of experience, scope of responsibilities — without sharing the internal document.
